_comment: P2-8 TensorRT-LLM bodies EN（2026-11-03）。sections 与源侧固定小节对齐；sources 按索引对齐 frontmatter。

axes.model_access: An LLM inference toolkit for NVIDIA GPUs: model definitions go through a Python API and trtllm-serve exposes a serving endpoint; the supported-model list follows official docs and is not enumerated here.
axes.runtime: Compile then serve: the model is compiled into a TensorRT engine and exposed through trtllm-serve with an OpenAI-compatible interface; the official positioning is large-scale data-centre/cloud deployment.
axes.local_files: Self-hosted, with weights and engines in your own environment; NVIDIA GPUs only, with CPU/AMD acceleration outside the official support scope.
axes.background: A long-running service suited to batching and high concurrency; no official statement of continuing after shutdown.
axes.tools: trtllm-serve provides the API; tool-calling and MCP support not verified item by item.
axes.context: Long context depends on model and VRAM; KV-cache optimisation lives in official docs, not verified item by item.
axes.permissions: Self-hosted with no account system; authentication, quotas and multi-tenant isolation are configured by the deployer.
axes.fit: Fits NVIDIA GPU clusters that need production throughput and low latency and already have container/compile pipelines. Does not fit single-card consumer setups, AMD/CPU deployment, or download-and-run GGUF workflows.

runs: This site has not completed throughput or VRAM tests; the conclusions cover runtime capability and licensing only.
unknowns:
- Current supported-model list (official docs are authoritative; not enumerated here)
- Tool-calling and MCP support status
- Compile time and engine size per release
related: Both are serving engines; vLLM targets general GPUs while TensorRT-LLM focuses on NVIDIA compilation.
Another high-throughput serving route to read in contrast.
